title: Ravi's First Crash
character: Ravi, 26, first salaried job in Mangaluru
source: yfinance 2026-09-08: NIFTY 23,682.50 (-3.67% 30d); S&P 500 7,718.60 (-0.06% 30d); BANK NIFTY 56,963.75 (-1.25%); BTC $78,877 (+21.53%) | beat6-7 math: phone tick = 48165*(nifty/23682) -> 53,286 at full recovery (+6.57% vs 50k start; VO says 'fifty three thousand, up six and a half percent' = honest rounding) — number-lock verified

beats.vo: Ravi is twenty-six. First salary job in Mangaluru. He put fifty thousand rupees into an index fund — and honestly, he barely thought about it.

visual.note: story starts with RAVI: savings graph 0->50k, no index ticker

beats.vo: Then one Tuesday, the NIFTY is down three point six seven percent in a month. Twenty three thousand six hundred eighty two. Every news channel is screaming red.
beats.visual: zoom toward monitor: NIFTY 23,682 ▼ -3.67% red, ticker flickers

beats.vo: He opens his phone. Forty eight thousand one hundred sixty five. He has lost one thousand eight hundred thirty five rupees. His stomach drops.
beats.visual: zoom to phone: ₹48,165, then ▼ ₹1,835 red overlay, Ravi frown

beats.vo: He wants to sell everything. But look at the wider picture — the S&P five hundred is down zero point zero six percent. Bank Nifty, only minus one point two five. This is a dip, not a collapse.
beats.visual: split screen: NIFTY -3.67 vs S&P -0.06 vs BANK NIFTY -1.25, cardboard comparison cards drop in

beats.vo: Three rules keep him in the chair. One — a three percent dip is normal; the index has fallen ten percent or more many times and still recovered. Two — his money is in twenty five hundred companies, not one stock. Three — selling in a panic turns a paper loss into a real one.
beats.visual: three rule cards stamp in one by one: NORMAL / DIVERSIFIED / NEVER PANIC-SELL

beats.vo: He does nothing. That is the whole move. Months pass — the calendar flips — and the index climbs back to twenty six thousand two hundred.
beats.visual: calendar pages flip (SEP→APR), ticker climbs 23,682 → 26,200, Ravi smiles again

beats.vo: His fifty thousand is back to fifty three thousand — up six and a half percent from where he started, because he never sold. Ravi's first crash taught him the only lesson that matters: time in the market beats timing the market. Follow for the next story.
beats.visual: phone shows ₹53,285 green, Ravi smiles + thumbs up, CTA card
